specId: D2 a pending start is reported as already_running

referee.disposition: APPROVE design; extract + promote on schema, then send identity for GO. No mutant before approval of the carrier.

anchorResolution.note: UTF-16 offset, independently confirmed by referee and executor

guarantee: A second same-key caller arriving while a start is still pending JOINS that start and receives a usable url, rather than being handed status:'already_running' with url undefined.
discriminatorArgument: HONEST: the second call hits `if (existing.pendingStart) return existing.joinable;`, awaits the joinable, and receives the FIRST call's completed result -- url is a real url, toBeTruthy passes. HOSTILE: the branch is removed, control falls to `return { url: existing.url, port: existing.port, status: 'already_running' }` while `existing` is STILL the pending marker -- and that marker is `{ pendingStart, repoRoot, joinable }`, carrying no url or port at all. So url === undefined and toBeTruthy fails. The VALUE differs because of the mutation, not the ordering. Marker shape verified in source at dashboard.js:23-38, not assumed -- D1 failed precisely because I named an assertion whose value was identical in both worlds.
populationArgument: Three cases issue two graphDashboard calls. :256 and :332 both use `repoRoot: second` -- a DIFFERENT key -- so activeDashboards.get(repoRoot) returns undefined, `existing` is falsy, and the mutated branch is unreachable. Both also await their first call to completion, so no pending marker survives. Only :298 makes a second SAME-KEY call and explicitly waits for the marker to exist. Hence expectFailures 1.
leakPrediction: NO EBUSY and no second message. D2's mutation makes the second call return EARLY; it never starts a rival dashboard, so no extra server or DB handle is opened and teardown has nothing locked. FALSIFIABLE: if EBUSY appears, this leak model is wrong and the D1 diagnosis must be revisited too.
case: ★★ a SECOND same-key call joins the in-flight start, it is not told a lie
expect: the joiner must receive a usable url, never undefined

predictions.mutant: exit 1; EXACTLY ONE failing case (:298); ONE message containing the predicate

downstreamAssertionsUnexecuted: `b.url === a.url` and `started.toHaveLength(1)` both sit AFTER the predicted toBeTruthy throw. Vitest stops the case at the first throw, so they will be UNEXECUTED -- no verdict. They must not be reported as passing.
antiTargets: :256 or :332 failing -- the different-key reasoning is wrong
any EBUSY or second message -- the leak model is wrong
the 20-second case timeout -- a hang is not a witness
any beforeEach/afterEach throw or non-case error
any failing-case total other than exactly 1
restorationCarrier: detached disposable worktree at the approved commit; node_modules by recorded junction; the TRACKED spec consumed directly; restore verified by hash; worktree disposed
boundedClaim: A pass would establish that the pending-join branch is load-bearing for the same-key JOIN route. NOT teardown, NOT ownership, NOT release -- and NOT that the marker is published early enough, which is D1's separate and still-unwitnessed question.
